name: Basis state and phase effect scalar
summary: An X-spider with phase aπ connected to a Z-spider with phase α is the scalar √2 $e^{iaα}$.
description:
An X-spider with phase aπ, for a ∈ {0, 1}, is (up to √2) the computational basis state $|a\rangle$. Plugging it into the one-legged Z-spider with phase α, which is the effect $\langle 0| + e^{i\alpha}\langle 1|$, gives the scalar $\sqrt2\, e^{ia\alpha}$.

For a = 0 this says that a phase-free X-spider connected to *any* Z-phase is √2, so a Z-phase can be absorbed into such a scalar diagram. For a = 1 this gives a diagram for every scalar of modulus √2. These diagrams are the standard way to represent global phases in ZX-diagrams, for instance in [local complementation](../local-complementation/).
